title: Combining Two Statements
summary: Learn how two or more statements can be connected to reach a conclusion through a clear logical chain.
learningObjectives: Connect two related statements to form a logical chain
Use shared terms to identify relationships between groups
Draw conclusions that follow through more than one step
Recognize when two statements cannot be safely connected

contentBlocks.content: Some conclusions are not stated directly in a single sentence. They become clear only when two or more statements are connected. The key is to find a shared person, group or idea that links the statements.

contentBlocks.title: A simple chain
contentBlocks.content: Statements: All doctors are graduates. All graduates are educated. Conclusion: All doctors are educated. The group 'graduates' connects the two statements, so the conclusion follows through a two-step chain.

contentBlocks.title: The chain pattern
contentBlocks.content: If all A are B and all B are C, then all A are C. The middle group B acts as the bridge between A and C.

contentBlocks.title: Using 'some' in a chain
contentBlocks.content: Statements: Some students are athletes. All athletes are disciplined. Conclusion: Some students are disciplined. The students who are athletes must also be disciplined.

contentBlocks.title: Using 'no' in a chain
contentBlocks.content: Statements: All pilots in Unit A are trained professionals. No trained professionals in Unit A are unlicensed. Conclusion: No pilots in Unit A are unlicensed. The trained-professional group connects the two statements.

contentBlocks.title: Do not force a connection
contentBlocks.content: Statements: Some teachers are writers. Some writers are musicians. You cannot conclude that some teachers are musicians. The two 'some' groups may contain different writers.

contentBlocks.title: A safe method
items: Identify the subject and group in each statement.
Look for a shared term that can act as a bridge.
Follow the direction of each relationship.
Check whether the same members must continue through the chain.
Reject the conclusion if the connection is only possible rather than necessary.

contentBlocks.title: Check your understanding
contentBlocks.content: Statements: All auditors are accountants. All accountants understand financial records. Conclusion: All auditors understand financial records. Yes. The accountant group links auditors to people who understand financial records.

contentBlocks.title: Two 'some' statements need care
contentBlocks.content: The word 'some' does not identify the same individuals unless the statements force that connection. Never assume that two separate 'some' groups overlap.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson summary
contentBlocks.content: Logical chains allow you to combine statements through a shared term. A conclusion follows only when the connection is necessary. Follow the direction carefully and avoid assuming that separate 'some' groups refer to the same members.

contentBlocks.title: Key takeaways
items: A shared term can connect two statements.
All A are B and all B are C allows all A are C.
Some A are B and all B are C allows some A are C.
Separate 'some' statements do not automatically refer to the same members.
Every step in the chain must be logically guaranteed.
